## FundProfileScopeEndpointFilters

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Ui.Shared.Endpoints.FundProfileScopeEndpointFilters</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Ui.Shared/Endpoints/FundProfileScopeEndpointFilters.cs:37](../../../../src/Meridian.Ui.Shared/Endpoints/FundProfileScopeEndpointFilters.cs#L37).

Endpoint filter that applies the fund-profile tenant ownership gate (SEC-005 slice 3) to fund-scoped read routes. When a request carries a fundProfileId query value that the authoritative IFundProfileTenantGuard reports as owned by a different tenant, the route is refused with 403 before any fund-partitioned data is loaded. Read-side counterpart to the governed-write guard on the Security Master workbench field-edit route. Its strictness follows the deployment&#x27;s TenantScopeEnforcementOptions. Under TenantScopeEnforcementMode.DeploymentBoundary it is fail-open: a blank fund, a caller with no tenant scope, a fund the registry does not positively attribute to another tenant, or an unavailable registry all pass — the single-company-per-deployment boundary remains the control and a legitimate read is never blocked. Under TenantScopeEnforcementMode.FailClosed each of those four becomes a refusal, because each is a scope that could not be resolved, and the exit criterion is categorical: an unresolvable scope is rejected rather than defaulted. The unavailable-registry case is the one most easily missed and the most important — a gate that cannot reach its authority has not decided that the caller is entitled, it has merely failed to ask. The tenantless-caller refusal is evaluated before the absent-fund short circuit, so omitting fundProfileId entirely is not a way past it. The routes attached to this filter have no separate tenant gate behind it, and their stores treat a null tenant with no fund as no filter at all — so under fail-closed the omission has to be refused here or nowhere. See docs/security/security-remediation-backlog.md (SEC-005) and W9-GOV-008 criterion 2.

```csharp
public static class FundProfileScopeEndpointFilters
```

Declared public members:

| Declaration | Source | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code>public static RouteHandlerBuilder RequireFundProfileTenantScope(this RouteHandlerBuilder builder, params UserPermission[] readPermissions);</code> | [src/Meridian.Ui.Shared/Endpoints/FundProfileScopeEndpointFilters.cs:52](../../../../src/Meridian.Ui.Shared/Endpoints/FundProfileScopeEndpointFilters.cs#L52) | Adds the fund-profile tenant ownership gate to a fund-scoped read endpoint. The gate reads the fundProfileId query value and denies only a fund positively owned by another tenant. Pass the route&#x27;s read permission(s) so the ownership check runs only for callers who can already read this route. Endpoint filters execute before the route delegate&#x27;s own permission check, so without this an unauthorized caller would receive the ownership 403 for a foreign fund but fall through to the handler&#x27;s plain 403 for an own/unbound fund — distinguishing cross-tenant ownership to callers who should see neither. When no permissions are supplied the check always runs (the route has no read gate to defer to). |

## IFundProfileTenantGuard

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Ui.Shared.Endpoints.IFundProfileTenantGuard</code>. Kind: `interface`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Ui.Shared/Endpoints/IFundProfileTenantGuard.cs:19](../../../../src/Meridian.Ui.Shared/Endpoints/IFundProfileTenantGuard.cs#L19).

Defense-in-depth guard for body-supplied fund-profile scopes on governed Security Master writes. The platform&#x27;s tenant isolation is enforced by the single-company-per-deployment boundary (today TenantId == CompanyId; the fund-scoped stores — strategy runs, ledger books, report packs — partition by FundProfileId alone, not by tenant). That boundary is the control; see docs/security/security-remediation-backlog.md (SEC-005) for the tracked storage-enforced isolation follow-up. This guard is not that boundary. It is a tripwire that refuses a fund-profile id which demonstrably belongs to a different company. It deliberately allows a fund the caller already uses, a fund unknown to every company, and the case where the backing authority is unavailable, so a legitimate edit is never blocked (no false-deny). Under the current single-company runtime it never fires; it only bites if a future multi-tenant, shared-datastore deployment co-locates several companies&#x27; funds.

```csharp
public interface IFundProfileTenantGuard
```

| <code>Task&lt;FundProfileTenantDecision&gt; EvaluateAsync(WorkstationTenantContext tenant, string? fundProfileId, CancellationToken ct = default);</code> | [src/Meridian.Ui.Shared/Endpoints/IFundProfileTenantGuard.cs:28](../../../../src/Meridian.Ui.Shared/Endpoints/IFundProfileTenantGuard.cs#L28) | Evaluates whether fundProfileId may be used under the caller&#x27;s tenant/company context. Returns allowed for a blank scope, a fund the caller has touched, a fund unknown to every company, or when the backing authority is unavailable (the deployment boundary remains the control). Returns denied only when the fund has tenant-attributed history exclusively under other companies. |

## LoginSessionMiddleware

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Ui.Shared.Endpoints.LoginSessionMiddleware</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Ui.Shared/Endpoints/LoginSessionMiddleware.cs:27](../../../../src/Meridian.Ui.Shared/Endpoints/LoginSessionMiddleware.cs#L27).

Middleware that enforces session-based authentication. Sanitized lifecycle probes (/healthz, /readyz, /livez) and the loopback-scoped Prometheus scrape path (/metrics) are always exempt. The initial-account bootstrap surface (/setup/account, /api/auth/bootstrap) is exempt while no account exists; those endpoints gate themselves on the loopback-only, one-use MDC_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN. The login page (/login) and auth API endpoints (/api/auth/*) are exempt when authentication is configured. Unauthenticated API requests receive a 401 JSON response. Unauthenticated browser (non-/api) requests are redirected to /login. Authentication is optional in Development/Test and required elsewhere by default.

## MutationAuthorizationGuardMiddleware

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Ui.Shared.Endpoints.MutationAuthorizationGuardMiddleware</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Ui.Shared/Endpoints/MutationAuthorizationGuardMiddleware.cs:36](../../../../src/Meridian.Ui.Shared/Endpoints/MutationAuthorizationGuardMiddleware.cs#L36).

Enforces every mutating route&#x27;s declared authorization from in front of minimal-API argument binding, and refuses a mutating route that declares nothing. The endpoint filters attached by RequirePermission/RequireAnyPermission run only after binding has parsed the request body and resolved the handler&#x27;s services, so a caller holding zero permissions could learn validation outcomes (a binding 400) or trip service resolution before authorization was ever consulted. This middleware reads the same EndpointAuthorizationMetadata those filters record and answers 401/403 before any body byte is deserialized, mirroring the filters&#x27; own response bodies exactly. The filters stay attached as the declarative, host-independent layer, which means a host composed without this guard still fails closed once binding completes. Omission fails closed: a mutating route carrying no authorization declaration at all is refused outright unless it explicitly states why it needs none — EndpointPermissionlessMutationMetadata for deliberately permissionless seams (login, the first-account bootstrap, 410 Gone tombstones) or EndpointIndependentAuthenticationMetadata for routes that authenticate their caller by their own mechanism (provider webhooks, the portal grant exchange, the loopback lifecycle token). An empty-permission declaration (the RequireAuthenticatedSession family) passes through to its own filter, which owns the session-kind nuance a permission snapshot cannot express. Reads are deliberately out of scope; their posture is owned by the read-declaration lane.

```csharp
public sealed class MutationAuthorizationGuardMiddleware
```
